concept.title: Path travelled is not start-to-finish change
concept.inferential_jump: Distance counts the whole route travelled, while displacement records only the directed change from start to finish; a return to the start leaves zero displacement after a nonzero journey.
entry_assumptions: Can trace a route from a marked start to a marked finish on a straight line.

teaching_path.action: Mark a start point on a straight path and declare east as the positive direction.
teaching_path.why_valid: A directed change is only readable once the line has a stated positive way.
teaching_path.output: start: S.  east: positive.  west: opposite.

teaching_path.action: Trace a walk away from S and then back to S, counting every part of the route.
teaching_path.why_valid: The route count accumulates what was travelled even though the final place can match the initial place.
teaching_path.output: route travelled: nonzero.  start-to-finish change: zero because finish = S.

teaching_path.action: Compare that return trip with a one-way trip chosen to have the same total route length.
teaching_path.why_valid: Holding route length fixed while changing the finish isolates the information displacement carries.
teaching_path.output: same route length; different finish -> different displacement.

predict.prompt: A person walks away from a marker and later returns exactly to it. Before naming any quantities, has every measure of the journey returned to zero?
predict.defensible_answer: No. The start-to-finish change is zero, but the travelled route is still nonzero.

attempt.produces: Two short descriptions of the same return trip: one that records the whole route and one that records only start versus finish.

rubric.evidence_of: Keeping travelled path information after the return.
Using endpoints rather than retracing the route for displacement.

accepted: 'The traveller covered a nonzero route, but finished where they started, so the endpoint change is zero.'
rejected: 'Both are zero because the traveller ended where they began.' This erases the path that was actually travelled.

route.ask: Did the traveller move along any part of the path before returning?
route.why_this_ask: It makes the existence of travelled path undeniable before the endpoint comparison is introduced.

route.ask: Where is the finish compared with the start?
route.why_this_ask: It switches from the history of the route to the endpoint relation.

route.ask: Which description should keep the detour: the whole route or the start-to-finish change?
route.why_this_ask: The learner has to assign the two pieces of information to different quantities rather than memorize names.

route.ask: If another route has the same total travel but ends elsewhere, which description must change?
route.why_this_ask: The comparison tests whether the endpoint information has actually been separated from path length.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: The teaching path labels the two descriptions after a constructed return trip. The learner route first notices the contradiction between real travel and a zero endpoint change, then assigns each description a job.

boundary_test.prompt: If the traveller never leaves the starting marker, what happens to both descriptions?
boundary_test.answer: Both are zero: there is no travelled route and no change between start and finish.
boundary_test.confirms: The two quantities can agree in a boundary case without becoming the same concept.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Distance travelled and displacement are always the same number.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A walker leaves a marker, turns around, and finishes back at the marker. Is the journey length zero just because the final change in position is zero?
misconceptions.repair: Count every part of the route for distance; compare only the start and finish for displacement, keeping the declared direction.

exit_task.prompt: Route A leaves a marker and returns to it. Route B travels the same total amount but ends away from the marker. Without calculating a value, compare their distance and displacement.

answer.summary: The routes can have the same distance, but Route A has zero displacement while Route B has a nonzero directed displacement.
reasoning: Distance follows the whole route, so equal total travel can give equal distance.
Displacement compares only the finish with the start.
Returning to the marker erases the start-to-finish change, not the travelled route.
answer.check: Ignore the middle of each route and look only at the two endpoints; only Route A has matching endpoints.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The response makes only qualitative zero/nonzero and same/different comparisons; it asserts no computed magnitude.
